promise-return.feedback: The next callback receives the previous callback’s returned value. Logging without returning loses that value.

promise-next.feedback: Pass a callback that receives the name. Calling console.log while constructing the chain does not install that callback.

promise-reject.feedback: A catch callback handles rejection. A fulfillment-only then does not cover the failure branch.

promise-trace.feedback: Synchronous start and ready are logged before the queued fulfillment callbacks. This is a fixture, not a timing claim about arbitrary networks.

fetch-status.feedback: An HTTP error can still produce a response. Check response.ok before treating it as successful.

fetch-json.feedback: response.json() returns a promise. Await the parsed body before using its fields.

fetch-return.feedback: Use the parsed body rather than a response object property. This fixture assumes the documented { name } shape; broader validation is outside its scope.

fetch-trace.feedback: The explicit response.ok guard throws. fetch does not automatically reject solely because the HTTP status is 404.

display-loading.feedback: A loading message distinguishes a pending request from an empty or successful result.

display-text.feedback: textContent displays the name as text rather than parsing it as markup. This does not establish broader application security.

display-error.feedback: Keep an honest error message instead of silence or a success message when loading fails.

display-trace.feedback: The catch branch replaces the pending message with a visible failure message. This fixed trace does not test a deployed UI.
